title: Hy-Nomas: Tencent's open interactive world model
sources: https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.36729 (paper page and the author's comment, captured 2026-10-29)

segments.text: Tencent Hunyuan just released Hy-Nomas, an interactive world model you steer one turn at a time, with text and with the camera.
So here's an example. A panda climbs the stone pillars, and each new instruction changes what happens next in the same scene.
You can also mix the two. Describe the next moment in words, then choose how the camera sees it, like in this moon base.
A single world can keep going for up to sixty seconds of continuous video.

shot.highlight: Generate up to 60 seconds of continuous video

segments.text: It's an 8 billion parameter model, it outputs 720p, and it has a 360 thousand token context.
And it's built to remember. Look away, move on and come back, and the model carries objects and spatial context through the changing viewpoint.

shot.highlight: carries objects, environmental details, and spatial context through a changing viewpoint

segments.text: Here a large camera move returns to the original view, and the complex background is still there.
The technical report is out on arXiv, and it's on Hugging Face's papers page.

shot.to: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation

segments.text: Under the hood it's an 8B diffusion backbone that takes free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple turns.

shot.highlight: an 8B diffusion backbone that supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns

segments.text: And they're releasing the model weights, the code and the benchmarks.

shot.highlight: We release model weights, code and benchmarks

segments.text: In the comments, one of the authors says it supports the exact same features as Genie 4, but fully open source.

shot.highlight: Our model supports the exactly same features as Genie4

segments.text: Over on GitHub, they say it runs on a single RTX 4090 with low-memory inference, and you can fine-tune it with LoRA.

shot.highlight: It runs on a single RTX 4090 with low-memory inference

segments.text: People are already building on it, with integrations for ComfyUI, SGLang and WanGP.
One demo reports real-time 720p generation on a Google TPU slice with just four chips.

shot.highlight: real-time 720p generation on a v6e-4 slice (4 chips)

segments.text: There's a free demo you can try right now, and the official gallery has 83 generated worlds to browse.
